Raoul Pal on the Four-Year Window to Build Wealth, the Future of Crypto, and Why AI Changes Everything

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with @RaoulGMI, co-founder and CEO of @RealVision and founder of Global Macro Investor, for our sixth conversation to discuss the future of crypto, the accelerating impact of artificial intelligence, and why he believes the next four years could fundamentally reshape the global economy. We revisit his investment predictions, examine the thinking behind his controversial $SUI position, and explore what decades of navigating financial markets have taught him about conviction, patience, and building wealth. For Raoul, the opportunity ahead is extraordinary, but so are the consequences of getting left behind.

Why Doing Less Has Become Raoul's Investment Strategy

When we first spoke more than two years ago, Raoul was anticipating the arrival of the "Banana Zone," a period of explosive crypto price appreciation driven by expanding liquidity. That rally never materialized as he expected, but his underlying investment philosophy has barely changed.

Over the past year, Raoul has made just two purchases during significant market corrections, alongside adding a position in $ZEC. Rather than actively trading market cycles, he focuses on accumulating assets he believes will appreciate over longer periods. His principle comes down to compounding and the psychological difficulty of timing the market. Selling near a market peak might sound straightforward, but buying back after prices fall is considerably harder since investors are likely to hesitate, expect prices to decline further, and eventually find themselves watching prices recover from the sidelines.

Raoul uses deviations from long-term logarithmic price trends to identify moments when assets are particularly undervalued. Buying at depressed prices, such as accumulating Solana and Ethereum during the 2022 downturn, helped his portfolio recover to previous highs before the broader market did.

Understanding Liquidity and the Case for a Crypto Supercycle

Raoul acknowledges that the relationship between global liquidity and cryptocurrency prices has been weaker than he anticipated, as a disproportionate share of available capital has flowed into AI-related technology stocks. But he believes that situation could eventually reverse. More importantly, Raoul argues that stablecoins, tokenized assets, decentralized finance, and AI-powered transactions are creating new sources of demand for blockchain networks, and transforming crypto into essential financial infrastructure.

He considers @Ethereum and @Solana as established infrastructure networks, with other blockchains competing to become similarly important. His broader prediction is that crypto and technology could experience a prolonged supercycle extending toward 2030, resembling the accelerating technology boom of the late 1990s. That does not mean prices will rise uninterrupted. Severe corrections remain possible, but investors who focus exclusively on short-term volatility risk missing the longer-term structural transformation.

The SUI Bet and the Difference Between Conviction and Being Wrong

Still, he has maintained conviction because he believes only a handful of layer-one blockchains will eventually dominate the market for blockchain infrastructure. He sees @SuiNetwork as a potential contender because of its technology, transaction capabilities, and suitability for emerging applications. But he also recognizes that impressive technology alone does not guarantee success.

Here are the most important highlights from @Tesla's Q3 2026 earnings call:

• Tesla's 2027 Megapack production capacity is nearly sold out.

• Tesla is aiming to produce 5 million vehicles annually by 2030.

• Customers are increasingly visiting Tesla showrooms specifically to experience FSD rather than shopping for a particular vehicle model.

• Tesla said more than 75% of new North American vehicle deliveries included a paid FSD subscription signup, despite every vehicle already coming with a free one-month trial.

• FSD financial disclosure: Tesla plans to disclose additional FSD financial and operating metrics as the business scales, including subscription revenue and churn rates.

• Elon said Tesla is hoping for EU-wide FSD approval within a few months and would be surprised if approval takes longer than Q1 2027, although the timing depends on regulators.

• Unsupervised FSD for customer vehicles: Tesla expects to enable some customer-owned vehicles to participate in its autonomous Robotaxi network around Q2 2027, subject to fleet-management and geofencing requirements.

• Tesla is developing its own AI-based mapping and navigation system that will rely on intelligence gathered from its vehicle fleet rather than traditional third-party mapping systems. The system will support conversational voice commands, personalized routing preferences, improved parking, and more intelligent destination handling.

•  Tesla plans to launch Cybercab service in Dallas in November 2026, followed by additional cities.

• Tesla plans to progressively extend robotaxi operating hours, with the goal of reaching 24/7 service by the end of 2026. Tesla expects to expand service to highways, higher-speed roads, additional weather conditions, and nighttime operations by the end of 2026.

• Elon expects Robotaxi to begin making a noticeable contribution to Tesla's financial results around Q2 2027, potentially becoming a significant business by Q3 or Q4 2027.

• Tesla is targeting the first deliveries of Cybercabs to fleet owner customers by the end of 2026, but Elon said the vast majority of Cybercabs will be Tesla-owned and operated as transportation-as-a-service vehicles rather than sold directly to consumers.

• Tesla has started early Optimus production. Elon said: "The growth of Optimus is an S curve, but the initial curve is a shallow slope. There's still some things we need to tweak about the design. There's still quite a lot of work to do with the AI in the robot. I would expect that the AI, the electromechanical design, reliability, usage life, expect these issues to be solved by the end of next year."

• Elon said most of the equipment for an Optimus production line designed to manufacture approximately 1 million robots annually is already at Fremont. Elon expects it will take at least another year, possibly longer, to reach an annualized production rate of approximately 1 million Optimus robots, equivalent to roughly 20,000 per week.

• Elon said Tesla may release a new Optimus V3 demonstration video within one or two months, saying  that it should show genuinely AI-driven tasks rather than preprogrammed movements.

• Tesla is targeting mid-2027 to integrate its AI5 chip into Optimus.

• Management said Optimus production costs are trending toward the expected manufacturing cost of Cybercab, although the robot's design is still being refined.

• Tesla hopes to manufacture its first experimental semiconductor chips around May or June 2027. Tesla is targeting useful chip production at volume in Terafab around Q3 2028.

• Management expects higher Megapack average selling prices and further improvements in gross margins (currently 33%) as production expands.

You’ve been trading for over 3 years and it feels like you’ve just wasted your life.

You’ve tried it all. Forex. Options. Futures. Prop firms. Even Crypto.

Some of it worked for a while. You were hyped. Then the same habits caught up with you and you started blowing accounts again.

And now you’re not the 24-year-old with no mortgage, no kids, no real responsibilities anymore.

You’ve got a life now. Bills. A partner. Real pressure to provide.

So the stakes are different. You can’t afford to keep f*cking up in the markets.

Here’s what I’d tell you to do. Step by step.

1. Remove the pressure to make money.

Get a job, a side hustle, whatever. You need to remove the “I have to make money trading right now” pressure before anything else works.

2. Pick one thing and commit.

One market. One setup. One risk framework. And don’t touch anything else for a year.

3. Do less.

Stop watching every candle. Stop clicking buttons. Follow the plan and let the trade run according to the plan.

4. Find someone to hold you accountable.

A mentor, a partner, a community. Someone who acts as your manager, coach and reality check all at once. Be comfortable making progress alone… but don’t shut out opportunities that help you hit your goals faster.

5. Make decisions BEFORE the move.

Your job is to prepare to get in before you even see the move. Enter. Set your parameters. Walk away.

That’s how you become profitable and stay profitable.

Very happy to share a new paper, “Technology Bottlenecks: Measuring Where AI Could Raise the Value of Work It Cannot Yet Do.”

AI exposure measures ask about the work AI is capable of doing. We ask instead where the marginal value of work AI cannot yet do may rise as AI speeds up the rest of the job.

To do so, we employ 288 million U.S. job postings mapped line by line to their closest O*NET tasks and GPT-4 feasibility ratings from Eloundou et al. (2024) to construct a measure, “bottleneck pressure,” for each task in each occupation that posts it. 

Using a simple task-based framework, we derive this pressure at the task level, showing that for an AI-infeasible task it is the exposure of the occupation that posts it, so the same task can face very different bottleneck pressure in different jobs.

Reporting bottleneck pressure alongside AI exposure shows both the scope for AI to perform work and where improving the work it cannot do may pay off more as capabilities expand.

We formally announced Mirendil less than 4 months ago. Today, I'm excited to share an important milestone for:

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.

Mirendil's mission is to solve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) and use it to democratize frontier AI development, ultimately accelerating science and technology. At Mirendil, when we think about RSI, we think holistically about the company as an intelligent entity that self-improves toward its goal. From that perspective, the most powerful notion of acceleration is reducing the time and resources (number of human experts, compute, and other costs) needed to achieve ambitious goals.

Given that pretraining is perhaps the most important yet most challenging part of frontier AI development, we decided to run an ambitious controlled experiment: Starting fully from scratch, can we significantly reduce the time, number of human experts, and compute resources needed to go all the way to successfully pretraining a strong coding model at scale?

Mirendil-Base is the result of this experiment. Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute. This includes all the research and small-scale experiments it took to get there, as well as the final training run.

The recipe holds up as the models get bigger. For reference, Mirendil-Base is in the 100B-500B parameter range, Mirendil-Base-Large in the 500B-2T range, and Mirendil-Base-XL in the 2T-10T range.

We're beginning to see a world where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can take on work that once required an entire research organization. As these systems improve, the bottleneck shifts from the size of a team to the ambition and judgment of the people directing them. This has profound implications for who gets to build AI and, ultimately, who gets to push the frontiers of science and technology forward.

We’ll share independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks and API-access sooner than you think so stay tuned!

The thing, though, is that before AWS could scale and pull thru GCP and others as legitimate cash machines, there were a few clearing events to sort out these brittle revenues. 

This is the extrapolation of Ken’s point. We will need to transition from speculative AI spending to consistent, reliable spend that shows up in public market earnings reports.
